text:
anya: Heads-up — nightly eval (q8_1 bring-up) flagged a bunch of fncall JSON parse failures, 8/120 prompts. Looks like model is emitting comment markers inside tool output and our parser rejects it.

sam: Can you paste an example payload?

anya: Here is one of the raw tool outputs from the logs (copied verbatim):
```
{"function": "lookup", "args": {"query": "recent sales"}} // best guess: include time range
```

jordan: Whoa, the // comment is outside the JSON. Model clearly appended a human-style note. Parser blows up on that.

lina: Another variant we saw embeds a C-style comment inside a string field which is trickier: 
```
{"function":"format","args":"{\"date\":\"2025-09-01\"} /* generated by model */"}
```

anya: Repro steps I used: run nightly-eval --model q8_1-bringup --promptset regression_v2 --seed 42, filter for fncall failures, then tail the raw agent logs. Failures only show up for the quantized variant, not the fp16 baseline.

nightly-bot: nightly-eval-run 2168007000: 8 fncall-json errors, 0 crashes, regression flag set :warning:

sam: Hypothesis: tokenizer/decoder in the quantized runtime is merging token spans and the model emits explanatory fragments outside the JSON token stream. Could be prompting style too (we include "explain your choice" in some prompts).

jordan: Quick mitigation: strip trailing C/C++/JS comment patterns before JSON parse and log the stripped text for audit. But we need to record originals for eval reproducibility.

lina: Agreed. Also add a schema guard that rejects if args is a string that contains comment patterns and route to manual review.

anya: I'll open a triage issue with samples, model/commit, and repro commands and tag inference and evals. Assigning to @sam and @jordan to own immediate mitigation.

sam: OK will add a small sanitizer in nightly harness (non-destructive, writes original->sanitized artifact) and push a canary by EOD.

jordan: I'll update the eval dashboard to surface comment-like tokens per failure so we can track frequency over builds.

anya: Thanks — adding notes to the quant-qa doc. If mitigation reduces failures we can prioritize a deeper runtime fix. :thumbsup:
